articles.headline: Does Kubernetes DRA Replace HAMi?
articles.dek: Kubernetes is moving GPU allocation into the built‑in DRA webhook, which may make NVIDIA's HAMi custom resources obsolete.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Kubernetes is shifting GPU allocation to the native Device Resource Allocation (DRA) webhook, a move that could retire the separate NVIDIA HAMi CRDs for most workloads [FACT:eb68f38a5668129f5e9f27940eb193e3][FACT:f2a1ae18c549801f7215a318f229532a].
Why This Matters

Builders now using HAMi vGPU CRDs can switch to a standard "gpu" extended resource, dropping custom operator code and staying inside the core API surface [FACT:af8ad6b3003efac695cb884be5eb23a1][FACT:6bdfb14c04fbc1702a170386fdf1a65c].
What Happened

The CNCF blog explains that the DRA webhook hands out device IDs as opaque integers, while the NVIDIA device plugin still reports whole‑device counts [FACT:6bdfb14c04fbc1702a170386fdf1a65c][FACT:d1dd0df8a81b3ab2c31d395b7fb8f76d]. In HAMi, a vGPU might be allocated as device [NVIDIA: 8000] – a pattern DRA will emulate [FACT:67fafec14fc0008a5985f5ae05e06835].
Builder View

To adopt DRA, keep your pod spec unchanged but replace the custom HAMi resource name with the generic "gpu" extended resource; the webhook then binds the pod to a specific vGPU ID behind the scenes [FACT:f2a1ae18c549801f7215a318f229532a][FACT:6bdfb14c04fbc1702a170386fdf1a65c].
Ardur Take

The shift is documented in a single CNCF blog post, so confidence is moderate, but the alignment with Kubernetes’ own resource model suggests it’s worth testing DRA in a staging cluster before deprecating HAMi [FACT:eb68f38a5668129f5e9f27940eb193e3][FACT:f2a1ae18c549801f7215a318f229532a].

keyPoints: DRA webhook now allocates GPU device IDs as opaque integers [FACT:6bdfb14c04fbc1702a170386fdf1a65c]
NVIDIA device plugin still reports whole‑device counts, a mismatch DRA aims to resolve [FACT:d1dd0df8a81b3ab2c31d395b7fb8f76d]
HAMi vGPU allocations (e.g., [NVIDIA: 8000]) illustrate the pattern DRA will replace [FACT:67fafec14fc0008a5985f5ae05e06835]
articles.whyItMatters: GPU‑heavy workloads can move to a standard Kubernetes resource, reducing custom code and future‑proofing clusters against upstream changes [FACT:af8ad6b3003efac695cb884be5eb23a1].
articles.readerAction: Read the CNCF blog, enable the DRA feature gate in a test cluster, and verify that your GPU pods schedule with the generic "gpu" resource instead of HAMi CRDs [FACT:f2a1ae18c549801f7215a318f229532a].
